title: Even Higher-Level Overview

html:
Fully combine the stages, creating another cheat sheet

Egocentric, concrete sensorimotor prediction -> egocentric, concrete sensorimotor and symbolic prediction -> depersonalized, concrete sensorimotor and symbolic prediction -> depersonalized, abstract sensorimotor and symbolic prediction

–

Phase 1: Core Knowledge Initialization

Pre-train with physics engine programs (intuitive physics)

Pre-train with planning/goal inference (intuitive psychology)

These serve as "start-up libraries" analogous to evolutionary endowment

Phase 2: Curriculum-Structured Learning

Present data in construct order (simple -> complex)

Enable caching of useful intermediate representations

Allow cached concepts to serve as primitives for composition

Phase 3: Active Learning Loop

while learning:

1. Generate hypotheses (programs) from current library 2. Select actions that maximize expected information gain 3. Observe outcomes 4. Update posterior over programs 5. Cache useful new programs/subprograms to library 6. Refactor library for efficiency Phase 4: Stochastic Search with Annealing

From the "theory learning as stochastic search" framework:

Start "hot" (high exploration, accept suboptimal proposals)

Gradually cool (exploitation, convergence to high-posterior theories)

Mirrors developmental trajectory: Children are more exploratory, adults more stable

–

Sensory/Motor (0-2 yrs): Minimizes error in basic perception. "Burnt in" (myelinated).

Parietal/Temporal (2-11 yrs): Minimizes error in concrete spatial/linguistic tasks. "Burnt in."

Prefrontal (11-25 yrs): Now that the lower layers are efficient "subroutines" that don’t require conscious monitoring, the Rostrolateral Prefrontal Cortex (RLPFC) wakes up. The RLPFC is the "apex" of the hierarchy. It takes the outputs of the concrete layers (concepts like "mass," "volume," "fairness") as its inputs. It doesn’t process sensory data; it processes representations of representations.

–

Stage 1 (Analogous to 0-2 years): Embodied Grounding and Intuitive Physics. The initial phase of training should focus on grounding the agent’s representations in physical reality. An agent, equipped with basic architectural priors (e.g., convolutional layers for vision, motor outputs for action) and core knowledge-like principles (e.g., object persistence), would be placed in a physically realistic, interactive simulation. Its learning would be driven not by extrinsic rewards, but by an intrinsic motivation module inspired by the PACE framework, rewarding the agent for exploration that reduces the prediction error of its nascent world model.

Goal: Learn a grounded, low-level, causal generative model of the physical world through self-supervised, embodied "play." Be able to render (even though it remains implicit) a full 3D map of a scene, fully segmented and complete with geometry, material properties, affordances, miscellaneous properties, and motion for each segment

Stage 2 (Analogous to 2-7 years): The Symbolic and Social Explosion. In the second stage, the agent would be introduced to language and social interaction. This could involve interacting with humans or other AI agents via natural language. The agent’s task would be to ground linguistic symbols in its sensorimotor experience (e.g., learning that the word "cube" corresponds to the visual and tactile properties of cubes it has manipulated). It would engage in more complex, goal-directed "play," both alone and with others, to test hypotheses. It would also begin to build a rudimentary Theory of Mind by learning to predict the actions of other simple agents based on their goals and observable knowledge.

Goal: Build a multimodal world model that links language to sensorimotor representations and includes basic predictive models of other agents.

Virtuous cycle between language learning and learning in all other modalities

Stage 3 (Analogous to 7 years - Adulthood): Abstract and Long-Horizon Reasoning. In the final stage, the agent’s full planning and control architecture (its "PFC") would be enabled. Leveraging its grounded, multimodal world model, the agent would be trained on tasks requiring complex, multi-step planning, counterfactual reasoning ("what if?"), and sophisticated collaboration in multi-agent social dilemmas. Its ToM would mature, allowing it to infer more complex latent states in other agents, facilitating more effective cooperation and competition.

Goal: Deploy the fully developed world model for flexible, abstract, and temporally extended goal-directed behavior in complex, open-ended environments.

Rule-based inference beyond simple association/co-occurence; proposing rules and testing them
